facts.text: Cottonwood Falls began in 1854 when Indian trader Seth Hayes established a cattle ranch near the Cottonwood River and Diamond Spring Creek.
By 1910 Cottonwood Falls sat at the junction of two Atchison, Topeka & Santa Fe Railroad lines, becoming a key market for farm produce.
The Chase County Historical Society now occupies the former Chase County National Bank, a building listed on the National Register of Historic Places.
Cottonwood Falls has endured numerous floods, most notably the Great Flood of 1951 that reshaped the Cottonwood River valley.
The Burnley Memorial Library, located on Oak Street, serves as a cultural hub and houses historic collections for Cottonwood Falls residents.
Nestled in the heart of the Flint Hills, Cottonwood Falls lies along the scenic Flint Hills National Scenic Byway, showcasing rolling prairie landscapes.
